# Python API

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_api_docs.py from the docstrings and Params fields of wgsextract_cli.api; do not edit. -->

The typed Python API of WGS Extract.

Every operation takes a frozen `*Params` dataclass and returns a
`Result` (the `wgsextract.result/1` manifest model the CLI writes):

```python
from pathlib import Path
from wgsextract_cli import api

res = api.vcf.snp(api.VcfSnpParams(input=Path("x.cram"), region="chrM"))
res.outputs, res.metrics, res.warnings
```

Operations raise `CommandFailed` (carrying the failed `Result`) unless
called with `check=False`. They accept a `progress` callback and a
`CancelToken`. Operations run one at a time per process. They write the same
output files and manifests as the CLI but print nothing to stdout: their
human-readable text is suppressed and external tools' stdout goes to stderr.
Stdout itself is left alone, so the caller's own writes (including from a
progress callback or other threads) still reach it, e.g. a stdio JSON-RPC server.

Unset fields with a config.toml setting take it, as on the CLI. The user's
config.toml is loaded on the first call; `use_config(path)` selects another.

The CLI is built on this layer: each migrated command's options are generated
from its Params fields, so the API and `--help` cannot drift.

Stability: the names exported here and the group modules (`api.extract`,
`api.info`, `api.bam`, `api.qc`, `api.align`, `api.vcf`,
`api.lineage`, `api.microarray`, `api.panel`, `api.report`, `api.sample`,
`api.support`) follow
semantic versioning from the 1.0 release; adding fields with defaults is not
a breaking change.
Modules whose names start with `_` are private and may change at any time.
See docs/api.md.

## Results, progress and cancellation

`api.Result` is the `CommandResult` model of the [result manifest](result-manifest.md): `status`, `exit_code`, `error`, `inputs`, `outputs`, `metrics`, `warnings`, `details`, `manifest` and `provenance`; `to_dict()` and `to_json()` give the `wgsextract.result/1` document. `api.json_schema(cls)` gives a JSON Schema of a Params class; `wgsextract help --all --json` includes it as each typed command's `input_schema`, with each property's flag as `x-cli-flag` (a positional argument's metavar as `x-cli-positional`).

### `api.ProgressEvent`

One progress report: a stage name, a message and, when known, how far
through the operation is (0.0 to 1.0).

Stages so far: `start` and `finish` (the command name, 0.0 and
1.0), `tool` (an external tool is starting), `step` (a resumable
workflow runs or skips one of its steps, and why) and `heartbeat` (a
periodic count from a long tool run, such as `"1,200/5,000 reads"`, with
the fraction of that run done when the total is known). More stages may be
added.

### `api.ProgressCallback`

Receives progress events, from the calling thread or a worker thread.

### `api.CancelToken`

Cooperative cancellation of a running operation.

`cancel()` may be called from any thread. It stops the operation's
external tools at once and makes the operation fail as cancelled at its
next checkpoint. A token belongs to one operation.

- `is_set`: Alias of `cancelled`, so a token works where a `threading.Event` does.
- `on_cancel`: Call `callback` on cancellation (at once if already cancelled); returns a function that unregisters it.

### `api.CommandFailed`

An operation failed; `result` holds the error, warnings and partial outputs.

## `api.info`

`info`: what a BAM/CRAM is (build, sequencer, sex, depth) and its coverage;
`info chip`: which microarray chip a raw-data file came from.

### `api.info.info(InfoParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract info`.

Describe a BAM/CRAM.

`details` holds the metrics (`ref_model_str`, `gender`,
`sequencer`, `avg_read_len`, `metrics`, ...); `metrics` holds the
headline numbers.

`InfoParams`: Identify the reference build, file integrity and sequencing metrics of a
BAM/CRAM. Metrics are cached next to the outputs as
`<input>.wgse_info.json`.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path` | required | `--input`, `-i` | BAM or CRAM to describe. |
| `ref` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `reference_fasta`) | `--ref` | Reference FASTA or reference library folder; resolved from the input's header when omitted (default: config reference_fasta). |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the input's folder). |
| `detailed` | `bool` | `False` | `--detailed` | Perform full index and body sample analysis (detailed mode) |
| `table_format` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--format` | Also save the per-chromosome table and the QC stats as <input>_chromosomes and <input>_qc .tsv or .parquet (needs pyarrow); implies --detailed. None saves no table. One of: `tsv`, `parquet` |
| `cache` | `bool` | `True` | `--cache` | Save the metrics as ``<input>.wgse_info.json`` for later runs; an existing cache is read either way. |

### `api.info.calculate_coverage(CalculateCoverageParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract info calculate-coverage`.

Exact coverage; outputs the coverage table (or the depth-bins TSV).

`CalculateCoverageParams`: Exact per-chromosome breadth and depth of coverage (`samtools coverage`).

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path` | required | `--input`, `-i` | BAM or CRAM to describe. |
| `ref` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `reference_fasta`) | `--ref` | Reference FASTA or reference library folder; resolved from the input's header when omitted (default: config reference_fasta). |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the input's folder). |
| `region` | `str \| None` | `None` | `-r`, `--region` | Chromosomal region (e.g. chrM, chrY:10000-20000) |
| `bins` | `bool` | `False` | `--bins` | Report exact per-contig depth 0, 1-3, 4-7 and 8+ breadth in one streaming pass. |
| `by` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--by` | Report depth per target of this BED (e.g. from 'panel bed'): mean, median and the fraction at >=10x, 20x, 30x and --min-depth, plus the on- versus off-target enrichment |
| `min_depth` | `int` | `30` | `--min-depth` | With --by, list targets whose mean depth is below this (default: 30) |
| `table_format` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--format` | Also save the per-chromosome table and the QC stats as <input>_chromosomes and <input>_qc .tsv or .parquet (needs pyarrow); implies --detailed; None saves none. With bins or by, that table's format instead (None: tsv). One of: `tsv`, `parquet` |

### `api.info.coverage_sample(CoverageSampleParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract info coverage-sample`.

Sampled coverage estimate; outputs the coverage table.

`CoverageSampleParams`: Estimated per-chromosome breadth of coverage from ~1,000 sampled windows.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path` | required | `--input`, `-i` | BAM or CRAM to describe. |
| `ref` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `reference_fasta`) | `--ref` | Reference FASTA or reference library folder; resolved from the input's header when omitted (default: config reference_fasta). |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the input's folder). |
| `region` | `str \| None` | `None` | `-r`, `--region` | Chromosomal region (e.g. chrM, chrY:10000-20000) |
| `table_format` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--format` | Also save the per-chromosome table and the QC stats as <input>_chromosomes and <input>_qc .tsv or .parquet (needs pyarrow); implies --detailed. None saves no table. One of: `tsv`, `parquet` |

### `api.info.chip(ChipParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract info chip`.

Identify a raw-data file's chip; `details` holds the candidates and
`metrics` the best `revision`, `match` and `confidence`.

`ChipParams`: Identify the vendor, chip and revision of a consumer microarray
raw-data file, or list the catalogued revisions.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--input`, `-i` | Microarray raw-data file; required unless list_revisions. |
| `ref` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `reference_fasta`) | `--ref` | Reference FASTA or reference library folder; resolved from the input's header when omitted (default: config reference_fasta). |
| `list_revisions` | `bool` | `False` | `--list` | List the catalogued chip revisions and their matching templates. |

## `api.extract`

`extract`: pull chromosomes, regions or unmapped reads out of a BAM/CRAM
into smaller BAM, VCF or FASTA files.

Outputs are named after the input (`sample.bam` gives `sample_Y.bam`) and
written to `outdir`, else beside the input. Calling and consensus commands
(`mito_fasta`, `mito_vcf`, `ydna_vcf`) need the matching reference; the
others use it only to decode a CRAM.

### `api.extract.mito_fasta(MitoFastaParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract extract mito-fasta`.

Write the mitochondrial consensus FASTA (output role `mt_fasta`).

`MitoFastaParams`: The mitochondrial consensus sequence as `<input>_MT.fasta`: chrM
reads called haploid with bcftools and applied to the reference's chrM.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path` | required | `--input`, `-i` | BAM or CRAM to extract from. |
| `ref` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `reference_fasta`) | `--ref` | Reference FASTA or reference library folder; resolved from the input's header when omitted (default: config reference_fasta). |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the input's folder). |
| `threads` | `int \| None` | `None` (config `cpu_threads`) | `--threads`, `-t` | CPU threads; None picks a count for this machine (default: config cpu_threads, else auto). |
| `memory` | `str \| None` | `None` (config `memory_limit`) | `--memory`, `-m` | Memory limit per thread, e.g. '2G'; None picks a share of this machine's RAM (default: config memory_limit, else auto). |

### `api.extract.mito_vcf(MitoVcfParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract extract mito-vcf`.

Call mitochondrial variants (output role `mt_vcf`; the `variants`
metric counts them).

`MitoVcfParams`: Mitochondrial variants as `<input>_MT.vcf.gz`, called haploid.

### `api.extract.custom(CustomParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract extract custom`.

Extract the reads of a region, BED file or gene (output role
`region_bam`).

`CustomParams`: The reads in a region, a comma-separated list of regions, a BED file or a
gene as `<input>_<region>.bam`. `region` or `gene` is required.
Regions may come in any order and overlap: the BAM is coordinate-sorted
and holds each read once.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path` | required | `--input`, `-i` | BAM or CRAM to extract from. |
| `ref` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `reference_fasta`) | `--ref` | Reference FASTA or reference library folder; resolved from the input's header when omitted (default: config reference_fasta). |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the input's folder). |
| `threads` | `int \| None` | `None` (config `cpu_threads`) | `--threads`, `-t` | CPU threads; None picks a count for this machine (default: config cpu_threads, else auto). |
| `memory` | `str \| None` | `None` (config `memory_limit`) | `--memory`, `-m` | Memory limit per thread, e.g. '2G'; None picks a share of this machine's RAM (default: config memory_limit, else auto). |
| `region` | `str \| None` | `None` | `-r`, `--region` | Region (chrY:10000-20000), comma-separated regions, or a BED file. |
| `gene` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--gene` | A gene name (e.g. BRCA1) to extract, looked up in the reference library's gene map (hg19/hg38 only); the region wins when both are set. |

## `api.bam`

`bam`: sort, index, convert, merge and unalign BAM/CRAM files.

Outputs are named after the input (`sample.bam` gives `sample_sorted.bam`)
and written to `outdir`, else beside the input. A CRAM is read with the
matching reference: `ref`, else the one the input's header names in the
reference library.

### `api.bam.sort(BamSortParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract bam sort`.

Coordinate-sort and index (output role `sorted_alignment`).

`BamSortParams`: Coordinate-sort and index the input as `<input>_sorted.bam` (or
`.cram`), optionally limited to a region or gene. A whole-file sort first
checks that the temporary and final files fit on disk.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path` | required | `--input`, `-i` | BAM or CRAM file. |
| `ref` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `reference_fasta`) | `--ref` | Reference FASTA or reference library folder; resolved from the input's header when omitted (default: config reference_fasta). |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the input's folder). |
| `threads` | `int \| None` | `None` (config `cpu_threads`) | `--threads`, `-t` | CPU threads; None picks a count for this machine (default: config cpu_threads, else auto). |
| `memory` | `str \| None` | `None` (config `memory_limit`) | `--memory`, `-m` | Memory limit per thread, e.g. '2G'; None picks a share of this machine's RAM (default: config memory_limit, else auto). |
| `region` | `str \| None` | `None` | `-r`, `--region` | Region (chrY:10000-20000), comma-separated regions, or a BED file to limit the output to. |
| `gene` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--gene` | A gene name (e.g. BRCA1) to limit the output to, looked up in the reference library's gene map (hg19/hg38 only); the region wins when both are set. |

| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the input's folder). |
| `threads` | `int \| None` | `None` (config `cpu_threads`) | `--threads`, `-t` | CPU threads; None picks a count for this machine (default: config cpu_threads, else auto). |
| `region` | `str \| None` | `None` | `-r`, `--region` | Region (chrY:10000-20000), comma-separated regions, or a BED file to limit the output to. |
| `gene` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--gene` | A gene name (e.g. BRCA1) to limit the output to, looked up in the reference library's gene map (hg19/hg38 only); the region wins when both are set. |
| `cram_version` | `str` | `'3.0'` | `--cram-version` | CRAM version to output (default: 3.0 for better compatibility) One of: `2.1`, `3.0`, `3.1` |

### `api.bam.unalign(BamUnalignParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract bam unalign`.

Write FASTQs (output roles `fastq_r1`, `fastq_r2` and, with `se`,
`fastq_single`; the `read_groups` metric counts the input's).

`BamUnalignParams`: Write the reads back to paired FASTQs, name-sorted so mates line up.
Reads without a mate go to `se` when set. Warns when the input has more
than one read group, which FASTQ can't keep apart.

| `threads` | `int \| None` | `None` (config `cpu_threads`) | `--threads`, `-t` | CPU threads; None picks a count for this machine (default: config cpu_threads, else auto). |
| `memory` | `str \| None` | `None` (config `memory_limit`) | `--memory`, `-m` | Memory limit per thread, e.g. '2G'; None picks a share of this machine's RAM (default: config memory_limit, else auto). |
| `r1` | `str` | required | `--r1` | Read 1 FASTQ to write: a bare name goes in outdir, a path is used as given. |
| `r2` | `str` | required | `--r2` | Read 2 FASTQ to write: a bare name goes in outdir, a path is used as given. |
| `se` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--se` | FASTQ for reads without a mate to write: a bare name goes in outdir, a path is used as given. |
| `region` | `str \| None` | `None` | `-r`, `--region` | Region (chrY:10000-20000), comma-separated regions, or a BED file to limit the output to. |
| `gene` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--gene` | A gene name (e.g. BRCA1) to limit the output to, looked up in the reference library's gene map (hg19/hg38 only); the region wins when both are set. |

Identify the reference (the `reference_md5_signature` metric).

CLI: `wgsextract bam merge`.

Merge the inputs (output role `merged_alignment`; the
`merged_inputs` metric counts them).

`BamMergeParams`: Merge coordinate-sorted BAM/CRAM files aligned to the same reference
into one indexed file. Identical `@RG` lines in several inputs are one
read group; conflicting ones get distinct IDs, with a warning.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `inputs` | `tuple[Path, ...]` | required | `FILE` | Two or more coordinate-sorted BAM/CRAM files aligned to the same reference. |
| `output` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--output` | Output file name or path; a bare name goes in outdir (default: merged.bam, or merged.cram with cram). |
| `cram` | `bool` | `False` | `--cram` | Write CRAM instead of BAM. |
| `attach_rg` | `bool` | `False` | `--attach-rg` | Tag each read with a read group named after its input file, for inputs without @RG lines (so reads stay traceable to their lane). |
| `ref` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `reference_fasta`) | `--ref` | Reference FASTA or reference library folder; resolved from the input's header when omitted (default: config reference_fasta). |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the first input's folder). |
| `threads` | `int \| None` | `None` (config `cpu_threads`) | `--threads`, `-t` | CPU threads; None picks a count for this machine (default: config cpu_threads, else auto). |

### `api.bam.to_ubam(BamToUbamParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract bam to-ubam`.

Write the unaligned BAM (output role `unaligned_bam`).

`BamToUbamParams`: A queryname-sorted unaligned BAM, as GATK's pipelines start from, as
`<input>_unaligned.bam`: from an aligned `input` (read-describing tags

| `r2` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--r2` | Read 2 FASTQ for paired-end --r1. |
| `sample` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--sample` | Sample name (SM) for FASTQ input, or for a BAM/CRAM without @RG lines (default: the input file name). |
| `library` | `str` | `'lib1'` | `--library` | Library name (LB) for a new read group. |
| `platform` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--platform` | Sequencing platform (PL) for a new read group (default: detected from the read names). One of: `ILLUMINA`, `DNBSEQ`, `ELEMENT`, `ULTIMA`, `PACBIO`, `ONT`, `IONTORRENT`, `LS454`, `SOLID`, `CAPILLARY` |
| `ref` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `reference_fasta`) | `--ref` | Reference FASTA or reference library folder; resolved from the input's header when omitted (default: config reference_fasta). |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the input's folder). |
| `threads` | `int \| None` | `None` (config `cpu_threads`) | `--threads`, `-t` | CPU threads; None picks a count for this machine (default: config cpu_threads, else auto). |
| `memory` | `str \| None` | `None` (config `memory_limit`) | `--memory`, `-m` | Memory limit per thread, e.g. '2G'; None picks a share of this machine's RAM (default: config memory_limit, else auto). |

## `api.qc`

`qc`: quality reports for reads and variants, and fake test data.

`fastp` trims reads; `fastqc`, `vcf` and `multiqc` report on reads,
variants and earlier results. Outputs go to `outdir`, else beside the
input.

### `api.qc.fastp(FastpParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract qc fastp`.

Trim the reads (output roles `trimmed_fastq_r1`, `trimmed_fastq_r2`,
`fastp_report_json` and `fastp_report_html`).

`FastpParams`: Trim and filter reads with fastp into `<reads>_fp_1.fastq.gz` (and
`_fp_2` for pairs) plus JSON and HTML reports. The read counts, Q30
rate and duplication rate are metrics.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `r1` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--r1` | Read 1 FASTQ (required). |
| `r2` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--r2` | Read 2 FASTQ, for pairs. |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the R1 file's folder). |
| `threads` | `int \| None` | `None` (config `cpu_threads`) | `--threads`, `-t` | CPU threads; None picks a count for this machine (default: config cpu_threads, else auto). |

### `api.qc.fastqc(FastqcParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract qc fastqc`.

Run FastQC (output roles `fastqc_report_html` and `fastqc_report_zip`).

`FastqcParams`: A FastQC report on a FASTQ, BAM or SAM file as `<input>_fastqc.html`
and `.zip`. Module PASS/WARN/FAIL counts and the read count are metrics.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path` | required | `--input`, `-i` | FASTQ, BAM or SAM file. |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the input's folder). |
| `threads` | `int \| None` | `None` (config `cpu_threads`) | `--threads`, `-t` | CPU threads; None picks a count for this machine (default: config cpu_threads, else auto). |

### `api.qc.multiqc(MultiqcParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract qc multiqc`.

Write the MultiQC report (output role `multiqc_report`).

`MultiqcParams`: One MultiQC HTML report, `multiqc_report.html`, from FastQC reports,
`bcftools stats` files and WGS Extract result manifests. Runs offline,
with MultiQC's AI summaries off.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path` | required | `--input`, `-i` | A report or result manifest, or a folder searched for them. |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the input folder, or the input's folder). |
| `force` | `bool` | `False` | `--force` | Replace an existing report instead of failing. |

### `api.qc.multiqc_metrics(MultiqcMetricsParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract qc multiqc-metrics`.

Write the custom-content files (output role `multiqc_custom_content`).

`MultiqcMetricsParams`: MultiQC custom-content files (`wgsextract_*_mqc.json`) from the
metrics in WGS Extract result manifests; MultiQC isn't needed.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path` | required | `--input`, `-i` | A result manifest, or a folder searched for them. |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the input folder, or the input's folder). |

CLI: `wgsextract qc vcf`.

Write the VCF statistics (output role `vcf_stats`).

`QcVcfParams`: `bcftools stats` on a VCF as `<vcf>.vcfstats.txt`; record, SNP and

### `api.qc.fake_data(FakeDataParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract qc fake-data`.

Generate the fake data (output roles `reference`, `alignment`,
`variants`, `fastq_r1` and `fastq_r2`, by type).

`FakeDataParams`: Generate a small fake genome for tests: reference, reads and calls
named `fake*`, reproducible from `seed`. Uses the build's installed
reference when there is one.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `coverage` | `float` | `1.0` | `--coverage` | Coverage depth (e.g. 30.0) |
| `build` | `str` | `'hg38'` | `--build` | Human genome build naming convention. One of: `grch38`, `hg38`, `hs38`, `hs38d1`, `hs38d1v0`, `hs38dh`, `GRCh38`, `hs38DH`, `grch37`, `hg19`, `hg37`, `hs37`, `hs37d5`, `GRCh37`, `chm13`, `chm13v2`, `chm13v2.0`, `t2t`, `t2tv2`, `t2tv2.0`, `t2tv20`, `T2Tv20`, `T2Tv2`, `T2Tv2.0`, `CHM13`, `CHM13v2.0` |
| `types` | `str` | `'cram'` | `--type` | Comma-separated list of types to generate (vcf, cram, bam, fastq, all). Default: cram |
| `full_size` | `bool` | `False` | `--full-size` | Use real human chromosome lengths. The default scaled mode uses shorter chromosomes. |
| `legacy_bam` | `bool` | `False` | `--legacy-bam` | Use the older scaled fake BAM generator. Slower and unavailable with --full-size, but includes randomized placement and indel CIGARs. |
| `seed` | `int` | `42` | `--seed` | Random seed for reproducibility |
| `ref` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `reference_fasta`) | `--ref` | Reference FASTA or reference library folder; resolved from the input's header when omitted (default: config reference_fasta). |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the current folder). |

## `api.align`

`align` and `realign`: map reads to a reference as a sorted, indexed,
duplicate-marked BAM or CRAM.

Short reads go through bwa-mem2 or bwa and samblaster, long reads through
pbmm2 (PacBio) or minimap2, and Ultima reads through their own pipeline. The
output is named after the reads (`sample_R1.fastq.gz` and
`sample_R2.fastq.gz` give `sample_aligned.bam`) and written to
`outdir`, else beside the reads.

### `api.align.align(AlignParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract align`.

Align reads to a reference (see `AlignParams`).

`AlignParams`: Align FASTQ reads (or an unaligned BAM) to `ref` as
`<reads stem>_aligned.bam` (or `.cram`) with its index. `r1` is
required; the CLI's `--genome` may fill it in from a sample workspace.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `r1` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--r1` | Read 1 FASTQ (or an unaligned BAM/CRAM of the reads). |
| `r2` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--r2` | Read 2 FASTQ, for pairs. |
| `preset` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--preset` | minimap2 preset for non-BWA alignment. Defaults to map-hifi for PacBio and map-ont for ONT. One of: `sr`, `map-pb`, `map-hifi`, `map-ont`, `ccs`, `subread` |
| `platform` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--platform` | Sequencing platform; selects platform-specific alignment tooling (default: detected from read groups or read names, else illumina). One of: `illumina`, `dnbseq`, `ultima`, `pacbio`, `hifi`, `clr`, `ont`, `nanopore` |
| `aligner` | `str` | `'auto'` | `--aligner` | Aligner to use. Auto uses bwa-mem2 for short reads when the reference has its index (see `ref index`), else bwa; for long reads pbmm2 for PacBio when installed, otherwise minimap2. One of: `auto`, `bwa`, `bwa-mem2`, `minimap2`, `pbmm2` |
| `gpu` | `bool` | `False` | `--gpu` | Align on an NVIDIA GPU with Parabricks: BWA-MEM for short reads, minimap2 for HiFi (Linux, Docker; see README). ONT requires CPU alignment to retain MM/ML methylation tags. |
| `sample` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--sample` | Sample name for the read group (default: the reads' file name). |
| `long_read` | `bool` | `False` | `--long-read` | Treat the reads as long reads (PacBio/ONT) and align them with pbmm2 or minimap2. |
| `format` | `str` | `'BAM'` | `--format` | Output format: BAM or CRAM (written with the target reference). One of: `BAM`, `CRAM` |
| `input` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--input`, `-i` | An aligned BAM/CRAM of the same sample whose header picks the reference from the library when ref is unset. |
| `ref` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `reference_fasta`) | `--ref` | Reference FASTA or reference library folder; resolved from the input's header when omitted (default: config reference_fasta). |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the input's folder, else the reads'). |
| `threads` | `int \| None` | `None` (config `cpu_threads`) | `--threads`, `-t` | CPU threads; None picks a count for this machine (default: config cpu_threads, else auto). |
| `memory` | `str \| None` | `None` (config `memory_limit`) | `--memory`, `-m` | Memory limit per thread, e.g. '2G'; None picks a share of this machine's RAM (default: config memory_limit, else auto). |

### `api.align.realign(RealignParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract realign`.

Re-align a BAM/CRAM to a reference (see `RealignParams`).

`RealignParams`: Re-align a BAM/CRAM to `ref` (possibly a different build) as
`<input stem>_aligned.bam` (or `.cram`) with its index.

The reads are extracted to FASTQ first, or streamed into the aligner when
the machine has the memory; FASTQs from an earlier extraction (beside the
input or in `outdir`) or given as `r1`/`r2` are reused. Free disk
space is checked first. Completed steps (extract, align, index) are
recorded in `<output>.steps.json` and skipped on a rerun whose inputs,
settings and tools are unchanged.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `r1` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--r1` | Read 1 FASTQ already extracted from the input, to align instead of extracting it. |
| `r2` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--r2` | Read 2 FASTQ, with r1. |
| `aligner` | `str` | `'auto'` | `--aligner` | Aligner: auto, bwa, bwa-mem2, minimap2 or pbmm2, chosen as for align. One of: `auto`, `bwa`, `bwa-mem2`, `minimap2`, `pbmm2` |
| `gpu` | `bool` | `False` | `--gpu` | Align on an NVIDIA GPU with Parabricks: BWA-MEM for short reads, minimap2 for HiFi (Linux, Docker; see README). ONT requires CPU alignment to retain MM/ML methylation tags. |
| `platform` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--platform` | Sequencing platform (default: detected from read groups or read names, else illumina). One of: `illumina`, `dnbseq`, `ultima`, `pacbio`, `hifi`, `clr`, `ont`, `nanopore` |
| `preset` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--preset` | minimap2/pbmm2 preset. One of: `sr`, `map-pb`, `map-hifi`, `map-ont`, `ccs`, `subread` |
| `input_ref` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--input-ref` | Reference FASTA the input CRAM was encoded with (default: --ref when its sequence names, lengths and MD5s match the CRAM, else the FASTA in the reference library whose sequence dictionary matches). --ref is the reference to realign to. |
| `sample` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--sample` | Sample name to embed in read-group metadata. |
| `long_read` | `bool` | `False` | `--long-read` | Treat input as long-read data (PacBio/ONT). |
| `format` | `str` | `'BAM'` | `--format` | Output format: BAM or CRAM (written with the target reference). One of: `BAM`, `CRAM` |
| `keep_fastq` | `bool` | `False` | `--keep-fastq` | Keep the FASTQs extracted from --input after alignment (default: delete them). FASTQs passed with --r1/--r2 or reused from an earlier extraction are never deleted. |
| `force_extract` | `bool` | `False` | `--force-extract` | Re-extract FASTQs even if a matching pair already exists next to the BAM. |
| `no_preflight` | `bool` | `False` | `--no-preflight` | Skip the up-front disk space check (not recommended). |
| `restart` | `bool` | `False` | `--force`, `--no-resume` | Rerun every step, ignoring the steps an earlier run completed. |
| `force_steps` | `tuple[str, ...] \| None` | `None` | `--force-step` | Steps to rerun with the steps that use their outputs; None reruns none. Steps: extract, align, index. One of: `extract`, `align`, `index` |
| `dry_run` | `bool` | `False` | `--dry-run` | Log which steps would run or be skipped, and why, and run none. |
| `input` | `Path` | required | `--input`, `-i` | The aligned BAM or CRAM to realign. |
| `ref` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `reference_fasta`) | `--ref` | Reference FASTA or reference library folder; resolved from the input's header when omitted (default: config reference_fasta). |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the input's folder). |
| `threads` | `int \| None` | `None` (config `cpu_threads`) | `--threads`, `-t` | CPU threads; None picks a count for this machine (default: config cpu_threads, else auto). |
| `memory` | `str \| None` | `None` (config `memory_limit`) | `--memory`, `-m` | Memory limit per thread, e.g. '2G'; None picks a share of this machine's RAM (default: config memory_limit, else auto). |

## `api.vcf`

`vcf`: call variants, and annotate, filter, tabulate and analyse VCFs.

`snp` and `indel` call small variants from a BAM/CRAM with bcftools;
`freebayes`, `gatk`, `deepvariant` and `clair3` with those tools, and
`cnv` and `sv` call copy-number and structural variants. The other
operations read a VCF: `vcf_input`, else `input`. Their outputs go
to `outdir`, else beside that VCF. Annotators take their data file from the
field, else config.toml, else the reference library (`ref`); see
`wgsextract ref` to download it.

### `api.vcf.snp(VcfSnpParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract vcf snp`.

Call SNPs; the `snps` output carries the record count in its metrics.

`VcfSnpParams`: Call SNPs from a BAM/CRAM into `snps.vcf.gz`.

Ploidy comes from `ploidy` or `ploidy_file`, else the reference
library's ploidy file, else bcftools' built-in GRCh37/GRCh38 table.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path` | required | `--input`, `-i` | BAM or CRAM to call. |
| `ref` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `reference_fasta`) | `--ref` | Reference FASTA or reference library folder; resolved from the input's header when omitted (default: config reference_fasta). |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the input's folder). |
| `threads` | `int \| None` | `None` (config `cpu_threads`) | `--threads`, `-t` | CPU threads; None picks a count for this machine (default: config cpu_threads, else auto). |
| `ploidy_file` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--ploidy-file` | File defining ploidy per chromosome (auto-resolved from --ref if possible) |
| `ploidy` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--ploidy` | Predefined ploidy name or value |
| `region` | `str \| None` | `None` | `-r`, `--region` | Chromosomal region (e.g. chrM, chrY:10000-20000) |
| `parallel` | `bool` | `False` | `--parallel` | Call contigs in parallel with up to --threads workers. SNP calling then recalls the stretches with sites deeper than 255 reads in one stream, because bcftools subsamples them with one random stream per process, so the calls match the default single stream. |
| `qc_min_depth` | `float \| None` | `None` | `--qc-min-depth` | Warn below this mean depth for this run; 0 disables (default: config qc_min_diploid_depth 15, or qc_min_haploid_depth 3 for chrY/mtDNA) |

### `api.vcf.table(VcfTableParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract vcf table`.

Write the table (role `variant_table`) and database (`variant_database`);
`rows` is a metric.

`VcfTableParams`: One row per variant with its annotations, as `<stem>_variants.tsv`
(or `.parquet`) and an SQLite database.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--input`, `-i` | The VCF to read when ``vcf_input`` is unset. |
| `vcf_input` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--vcf-input` | The VCF to read; wins over ``input``. On the CLI, --vcf-input defaults to config default_input_vcf when --input isn't given. |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the VCF's folder). |
| `region` | `str \| None` | `None` | `-r`, `--region` | Only export this region (e.g. chr22). |
| `sample` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--sample` | Sample whose genotypes to use (default: the first). |
| `all_alleles` | `bool` | `False` | `--all-alleles` | Also export ALT alleles the sample doesn't carry (0/0 calls, no-calls, the other ALT of a 0/1 multi-allelic site). |

| `no_sqlite` | `bool` | `False` | `--no-sqlite` | Write only the table file. |

### `api.vcf.to_fasta(VcfToFastaParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract vcf to-fasta`.

Build the consensus (role `consensus_fasta`, and `liftover_chain` with
`chain`).

`VcfToFastaParams`: The reference with the VCF's variants applied, as
`<stem>_consensus.fa.gz` (and optionally a liftover chain).

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--input`, `-i` | The VCF to read when ``vcf_input`` is unset. |
| `vcf_input` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--vcf-input` | The VCF to read; wins over ``input``. On the CLI, --vcf-input defaults to config default_input_vcf when --input isn't given. |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the VCF's folder). |
| `ref` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `reference_fasta`) | `--ref` | Reference FASTA or reference library folder; resolved from the input's header when omitted (default: config reference_fasta). |
| `threads` | `int \| None` | `None` (config `cpu_threads`) | `--threads`, `-t` | CPU threads; None picks a count for this machine (default: config cpu_threads, else auto). |
| `region` | `str \| None` | `None` | `-r`, `--region` | Only build this region (e.g. chr21 or 21:30000000-31000000); default: the whole reference. |
| `sample` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--sample` | Sample to use from a multi-sample VCF. |
| `haplotype` | `str` | `'iupac'` | `--haplotype` | How genotypes are applied: iupac (default) writes heterozygous SNVs as IUPAC codes (e.g. R for A/G) and applies homozygous ALTs; alt applies every ALT; 1 or 2 applies that haplotype of a phased VCF (for unphased genotypes, the first or second allele, so 1 keeps the reference at heterozygous sites). One of: `iupac`, `alt`, `1`, `2` |
| `uncalled` | `str` | `'auto'` | `--uncalled` | What to write where the VCF has no passing call: n (an N), ref (the reference base), or auto (default): n for a gVCF, whose reference blocks say which positions were called, ref for a variant-only VCF. One of: `auto`, `n`, `ref` |
| `include_filtered` | `bool` | `False` | `--include-filtered` | Also apply variants whose FILTER is not PASS. |
| `mask` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--mask` | BED file of regions to replace with N (e.g. low coverage). |
| `chain` | `bool` | `False` | `--chain` | Also write a chain file mapping reference coordinates to the consensus (indels shift positions). |

### `api.vcf.trio(VcfTrioParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract vcf trio`.

Filter the trio; output roles `trio_<mode>` (and `trio_joint`,
`trio_denovo_isolated` from BAM/CRAMs).

`VcfTrioParams`: Calls matching an inheritance mode in a child and both parents, as
`trio_<mode>.vcf.gz`. Three VCFs are merged; three BAM/CRAMs are first
genotyped jointly from the reads (`trio_joint.vcf.gz`), which de novo
calls need.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--input`, `-i` | The VCF to read when ``vcf_input`` is unset. |
| `vcf_input` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--vcf-input` | The VCF to read; wins over ``input``. On the CLI, --vcf-input defaults to config default_input_vcf when --input isn't given. |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the VCF's folder). |
| `ref` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `reference_fasta`) | `--ref` | Reference FASTA or reference library folder; resolved from the input's header when omitted (default: config reference_fasta). |
| `threads` | `int \| None` | `None` (config `cpu_threads`) | `--threads`, `-t` | CPU threads; None picks a count for this machine (default: config cpu_threads, else auto). |
| `mother` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `mother_vcf_path`) | `--mother` | The mother's VCF, or BAM/CRAM, for trio analysis. |
| `father` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `father_vcf_path`) | `--father` | The father's VCF, or BAM/CRAM, for trio analysis. |
| `proband` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--proband` | The child's VCF or BAM/CRAM; overrides --vcf-input/--input and configured defaults. With the parents' BAM/CRAMs, genotyped jointly from the reads, which de novo calls need. |
| `mode` | `str` | `'denovo'` | `--mode` | Inheritance mode to filter for. One of: `denovo`, `recessive`, `comphet`, `all` |
| `min_depth` | `int \| None` | `None` | `--min-depth` | BAM/CRAM input: minimum read depth in each person at a reported site (default 15) |
| `proband_sex` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--proband-sex` | BAM/CRAM input: the child's sex, for chrX ploidy (default: inferred from chrX/chrY coverage) One of: `male`, `female` |
| `region` | `str \| None` | `None` | `-r`, `--region` | Chromosomal region |

### `api.vcf.sv(VcfSvParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract vcf sv`.

Call SVs; output role `structural_variants`, and the `caller`
metric names the tool chosen.

`VcfSvParams`: Call structural variants into `sv.vcf.gz` (delly), `pbsv.vcf.gz`
or `sniffles.vcf.gz`.

`caller` picks the tool; otherwise Sniffles for ONT input (detected or
`ont`) and long reads, pbsv (else Sniffles) for `pacbio`, else delly.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path` | required | `--input`, `-i` | BAM or CRAM to call. |
| `ref` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `reference_fasta`) | `--ref` | Reference FASTA or reference library folder; resolved from the input's header when omitted (default: config reference_fasta). |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the input's folder). |
| `threads` | `int \| None` | `None` (config `cpu_threads`) | `--threads`, `-t` | CPU threads; None picks a count for this machine (default: config cpu_threads, else auto). |
| `region` | `str \| None` | `None` | `-r`, `--region` | Chromosomal region |
| `caller` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--caller` | SV caller to use (default: sniffles for detected ONT, else delly; pbsv/sniffles with --pacbio; sniffles with --ont or --long-read). pbsv is PacBio-only and is refused for ONT reads. One of: `delly`, `pbsv`, `sniffles` |
| `pacbio` | `bool` | `False` | `--pacbio` | PacBio HiFi/CCS data: use pbsv (or sniffles if pbsv is missing) with CCS thresholds. |
| `ont` | `bool` | `False` | `--ont` | Oxford Nanopore data: use Sniffles (detected ONT input selects it automatically). |
| `long_read` | `bool` | `False` | `--long-read` | Long-read data from any platform: use Sniffles unless --caller selects pbsv for PacBio reads. |
| `ccs` | `bool` | `False` | `--ccs` | Use pbsv CCS/HiFi thresholds when --caller pbsv is selected. |
| `tandem_repeats` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--tandem-repeats` | Optional tandem-repeat BED for pbsv discover or Sniffles (recommended for long-read SV calling). |
| `qc_min_depth` | `float \| None` | `None` | `--qc-min-depth` | Warn below this mean depth for this run; 0 disables (default: config qc_min_diploid_depth 15, or qc_min_haploid_depth 3 for chrY/mtDNA) |

| `input` | `Path` | required | `--input`, `-i` | BAM or CRAM to call. |
| `ref` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `reference_fasta`) | `--ref` | Reference FASTA or reference library folder; resolved from the input's header when omitted (default: config reference_fasta). |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the input's folder). |

### `api.vcf.deepvariant(VcfDeepvariantParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract vcf deepvariant`.

Call with DeepVariant; output role `variants`.

`VcfDeepvariantParams`: Call small variants with DeepVariant into `deepvariant.vcf.gz`.

The model follows `ont`, `pacbio`, `model_type` and `wes`, else the
reads (ONT_R104 for ONT, ULTIMA for flow-tagged Ultima reads, else WGS).
The CPU version runs in stages that a rerun resumes; `gpu` runs
Parabricks in one step.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path` | required | `--input`, `-i` | BAM or CRAM to call. |
| `ref` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `reference_fasta`) | `--ref` | Reference FASTA or reference library folder; resolved from the input's header when omitted (default: config reference_fasta). |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the input's folder). |
| `threads` | `int \| None` | `None` (config `cpu_threads`) | `--threads`, `-t` | CPU threads; None picks a count for this machine (default: config cpu_threads, else auto). |
| `region` | `str \| None` | `None` | `-r`, `--region` | Region(s) to call (e.g. chrM) or BED files of them, separated by spaces (commas with gpu). |
| `wes` | `bool` | `False` | `--wes` | Set model type to WES (default: WGS) |
| `model_type` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--model-type` | DeepVariant model type (default: ONT_R104 for detected ONT, ULTIMA for Ultima reads with their flow tags, else WGS). ONT_R104 supports R10.4.1 only and requires x86-64; Linux ARM64 supports WGS only. Use PACBIO for PacBio HiFi/CCS alignments. One of: `WGS`, `WES`, `PACBIO`, `HYBRID_PACBIO_ILLUMINA`, `ULTIMA`, `ONT_R104` |
| `ont` | `bool` | `False` | `--ont` | Alias for --model-type ONT_R104 (R10.4.1 only; x86-64). |
| `pacbio` | `bool` | `False` | `--pacbio` | Alias for --model-type PACBIO. |
| `checkpoint` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--checkpoint` | A custom model: its directory, or a checkpoint prefix. |
| `batch_size` | `int \| None` | `None` | `--batch-size` | CPU inference batch size (upstream default: 1024). Use 256 to lower TensorFlow peak RAM without changing models or precision; --threads controls make_examples shards, not this batch. |
| `gpu` | `bool` | `False` | `--gpu` | Call on an NVIDIA GPU with Parabricks (Linux, Docker; see README). |
| `qc_min_depth` | `float \| None` | `None` | `--qc-min-depth` | Warn below this mean depth for this run; 0 disables (default: config qc_min_diploid_depth 15, or qc_min_haploid_depth 3 for chrY/mtDNA) |
| `restart` | `bool` | `False` | `--force`, `--no-resume` | Rerun every step, ignoring the steps an earlier run completed. |
| `force_steps` | `tuple[str, ...] \| None` | `None` | `--force-step` | Steps to rerun with the steps that use their outputs; None reruns none. Steps: stage_reads, make_examples, call_variants, postprocess_variants. One of: `stage_reads`, `make_examples`, `call_variants`, `postprocess_variants` |
| `dry_run` | `bool` | `False` | `--dry-run` | Log which steps would run or be skipped, and why, and run none. |

## `api.lineage`

`lineage`: mtDNA haplogroups (Haplogrep 3), Y haplogroups (native Yleaf)
and Y-STR repeat counts.

### `api.lineage.mt_haplogroup(MtHaplogroupParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract lineage mt-haplogroup`.

mtDNA haplogroup; `metrics` holds `haplogroup` and
`haplogroup_quality` (plus `mt_contamination` and
`mt_contamination_level` with `contamination`). `details` holds the
full Haplogrep row (`haplogrep`), `haplogrep_version`, the `tree`
(id, version, name) and the haplocheck row (`haplocheck`).

`MtHaplogroupParams`: Predict the mtDNA haplogroup with Haplogrep 3 from a BAM/CRAM (chrM is
called first; needs the reference) or a VCF. The report is
`haplogrep_results.txt` in the output folder. The chosen tree is
downloaded once into the reference library. With `contamination`,
haplocheck also checks the mtDNA for a mixture of two haplogroups and writes
`haplocheck_contamination.txt`.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path` | required | `--input`, `-i` | BAM, CRAM or VCF with chrM/MT. |
| `ref` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `reference_fasta`) | `--ref` | Reference FASTA or reference library folder; resolved from the input's header when omitted (default: config reference_fasta). |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the input's folder). |
| `tree` | `str \| None` | `None` (config `haplogrep_tree`) | `--tree` | Haplogrep 3 tree (default: config haplogrep_tree, else phylotree-fu-rcrs, PhyloTree 17 Forensic Update). phylotree-rcrs is PhyloTree 17; mitotree-rcrs is FamilyTreeDNA Mitotree (non-commercial use only). One of: `phylotree-fu-rcrs`, `phylotree-rcrs`, `mitotree-rcrs` |
| `contamination` | `bool` | `False` | `--contamination` | Also check for mtDNA contamination with haplocheck. VCF input needs heteroplasmy levels (FORMAT/AF). |
| `threads` | `int \| None` | `None` (config `cpu_threads`) | `--threads`, `-t` | CPU threads; None picks a count for this machine (default: config cpu_threads, else auto). |
| `haplogrep_path` | `str \| None` | `None` (config `haplogrep_executable`) | `--haplogrep-path` | Path to the Haplogrep 3 executable or JAR (optional if in PATH) |
| `haplocheck_path` | `str \| None` | `None` (config `haplocheck_executable`) | `--haplocheck-path` | Path to the haplocheck executable or JAR (optional if in PATH) |
| `qc_min_depth` | `float \| None` | `None` | `--qc-min-depth` | Warn below this mean depth for this run; 0 disables (default: config qc_min_diploid_depth 15, or qc_min_haploid_depth 3 for chrY/mtDNA) |

### `api.lineage.y_haplogroup(YHaplogroupParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract lineage y-haplogroup`.

Y haplogroup; `metrics` holds `haplogroup`, `haplogroup_marker` and
`qc_score`, `details["predictions"]` every Yleaf prediction row and
`details["tree"]` the tree's `id`, `name`, `version`, `date` and
`license`.

`YHaplogroupParams`: Predict the Y haplogroup with the bundled native Yleaf from a BAM, CRAM
or single-sample VCF/BCF. Outputs go to `yleaf/` in the output folder.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path` | required | `--input`, `-i` | BAM, CRAM or single-sample VCF/BCF. |
| `ref` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `reference_fasta`) | `--ref` | Reference FASTA or reference library folder; resolved from the input's header when omitted (default: config reference_fasta). |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the input's folder). |
| `pos_file` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--pos-file` | Yleaf position file (optional) |
| `build` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--build` | Override the detected reference build for this run. One of: `hg19`, `hg38`, `t2t` |
| `tree` | `str \| None` | `None` (config `y_tree`) | `--tree` | Haplogroup tree: yfull (the pinned YFull YTree release), yfull_v10 (YFull 10.01), ftdna, isogg, or a config.toml [y_trees.<id>] tree (default: config y_tree, else yfull). |
| `tree_file` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--tree-file` | A Yleaf-format tree JSON to use instead of --tree, with its markers in --pos-file; QC1 backbone checks are skipped. |
| `min_reads` | `int` | `10` | `--min-reads` | Reads needed at a marker position for it to be used. |
| `base_quality` | `int` | `20` | `--base-quality` | Minimum base quality of a read at a marker position. |
| `base_majority` | `int` | `90` | `--base-majority` | Percentage of reads at a marker that must agree on the base. |
| `min_score` | `float` | `0.95` | `--min-score` | Minimum QC score of a reported haplogroup prediction. |
| `ancient` | `bool` | `False` | `--ancient` | Use ancient-DNA marker tables. |
| `no_ref_inference` | `bool` | `False` | `--no-ref-inference` | VCF: use genotyped positions only (targeted panels); otherwise --ref is required. |
| `qc_min_depth` | `float \| None` | `None` | `--qc-min-depth` | Warn below this mean depth for this run; 0 disables (default: config qc_min_diploid_depth 15, or qc_min_haploid_depth 3 for chrY/mtDNA) |

### `api.lineage.y_str(YStrParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract lineage y-str`.

Y-STR calls; `details["calls"]` lists every marker with its value and
read support.

`YStrParams`: Call Y-STR repeat counts from a BAM/CRAM into `ystr/` (a table and a
FamilyTreeDNA-order CSV).

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path` | required | `--input`, `-i` | Indexed BAM or CRAM. |
| `ref` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `reference_fasta`) | `--ref` | Reference FASTA or reference library folder; resolved from the input's header when omitted (default: config reference_fasta). |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the input's folder). |
| `panel` | `str` | `'Y-111'` | `--panel` | Marker panel: FamilyTreeDNA Y-12 to Y-111, PowerPlex Y23, Yfiler Plus, or all (default: Y-111). One of: `Y-12`, `Y-25`, `Y-37`, `Y-67`, `Y-111`, `PPY23`, `YfilerPlus`, `all` |
| `build` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--build` | Override the detected reference build for this run. One of: `hg19`, `hg38`, `t2t` |
| `min_reads` | `int` | `2` | `--min-reads` | Spanning reads needed to support a repeat count (default: 2). |
| `min_fraction` | `float` | `0.6` | `--min-fraction` | Share of spanning reads that must agree (default: 0.6). |
| `min_mapq` | `int` | `20` | `--min-mapq` | Minimum mapping quality for single-copy markers (default: 20). |

## `api.microarray`

`microarray`: consumer microarray (23andMe, AncestryDNA, ...) and AADR
files generated from a BAM/CRAM or VCF.

### `api.microarray.generate(MicroarrayParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract microarray`.

Generate the kits; each output carries its marker tallies in `metrics`.

`MicroarrayParams`: Generate a combined 23andMe-style kit and the selected vendor or AADR
formats from a BAM, CRAM or VCF.

Fields left at `None` fall back to config.toml (`microarray_*`
settings) and then to the documented default.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path` | required | `--input`, `-i` | BAM, CRAM or VCF to genotype. |
| `ref` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `reference_fasta`) | `--ref` | Reference FASTA or reference library folder; resolved from the input's header when omitted (default: config reference_fasta). |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the input's folder). |
| `threads` | `int \| None` | `None` (config `cpu_threads`) | `--threads`, `-t` | CPU threads; None picks a count for this machine (default: config cpu_threads, else auto). |
| `formats` | `str` | `'all'` | `--formats` | Comma-separated formats to generate, e.g. "23andme_v5,ancestry_v2" (default: "all", the combined kit only); see `wgsextract microarray --help` for the list. |
| `table_format` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--format` | Also save the genotypes as <input>_genotypes.tsv or .parquet (needs pyarrow): rsID, chrom, pos (in the input's build) and genotype. None saves no table. One of: `tsv`, `parquet` |
| `indel_manifest` | `tuple[str, ...]` | `[]` | `--indel-manifest` | Opt-in sequence-defined I/D probes from a matching GRCh37 Illumina CSV, gzip or ZIP; repeat per selected format |
| `strand_ambiguous` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--strand-ambiguous` | Keep/no-call biallelic A/T or C/G input SNPs; unknown probe alleles are not inferred (default: config or keep) One of: `keep`, `no-call` |
| `resolve_rsids` | `bool \| None` | `None` | `--resolve-rsids` | Resolve packaged dbSNP aliases and no-call retired/ambiguous marker IDs (default: config or false) |
| `quirks` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--quirks` | corrected: forward-strand calls; vendor: reverse-strand calls where a template's vendor revision reported them so (default: config or corrected) One of: `corrected`, `vendor` |
| `min_gq` | `int \| None` | `None` | `--min-gq` | Minimum sample GQ; missing GQ becomes a no-call (default: config or 0, disabled) |
| `min_dp` | `int \| None` | `None` | `--min-dp` | Minimum sample DP; missing DP becomes a no-call (default: config or 0, disabled) |
| `assume_hom_ref` | `bool \| None` | `None` | `--assume-hom-ref` | Assume absent VCF markers are reference on represented contigs (default: config or true) |
| `exclude_filtered` | `bool \| None` | `None` | `--exclude-filtered` | No-call VCF records failing FILTER (default: config or false) |
| `call_reasons` | `bool \| None` | `None` | `--call-reasons` | Also write CombinedKit_reasons.tsv with explicit reasons (default: config or false) |
| `aadr_sample_id` | `str` | `'sample'` | `--aadr-sample-id` | Non-identifying sample label for AADR .fam/.ind (default: sample) |
| `aadr_sex` | `str` | `'U'` | `--aadr-sex` | AADR metadata sex only; does not change genotype calling (default: U) One of: `U`, `M`, `F` |
| `parallel` | `bool \| None` | `None` | `--parallel` | Call chromosomes in parallel workers (default: on with --threads above 1; calls are identical to one stream) |
| `ref_vcf_tab` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--ref-vcf-tab` | Master tabulated list of all consumer microarray SNPs (auto-resolved from --ref if possible) |
| `ploidy_file` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--ploidy-file` | File defining ploidy per chromosome (auto-resolved from --ref if possible) |
| `sample` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--sample` | Sample to use from a multi-sample VCF (e.g. a joint-called nf-core/sarek VCF); required when the VCF has more than one |
| `region` | `str \| None` | `None` | `-r`, `--region` | Chromosomal region (e.g. chrM, chrY:10000-20000) |
| `qc_min_depth` | `float \| None` | `None` | `--qc-min-depth` | Warn below this mean depth for this run; 0 disables (default: config qc_min_diploid_depth 15, or qc_min_haploid_depth 3 for chrY/mtDNA) |

## `api.report`

`report`: a sample's results as one local HTML, Markdown and JSON report.

The report summarises what earlier runs left in the sample folder (their
result manifests and the sample workspace): overview and QC, lineage,
pharmacogenomics, ClinVar pathogenic calls in the ACMG SF genes and the
microarray export. It runs no analysis and makes no network calls:

```python
res = api.report.build(api.ReportParams(workspace=Path("HG002")))
report = res.details          # the wgsextract.report/1 document
```

Every finding has a confidence label, its evidence (file relative to the
sample folder, plus region) and the "technical result, not diagnosis"
disclaimer. See docs/personal-report.md.

### `api.report.build(ReportParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract report`.

Write the report. `details` is the `wgsextract.report/1` document;
`outputs` are the HTML (`report_html`), Markdown
(`report_markdown`), JSON (`report_json`) and findings table
(`findings_table`).

`ReportParams`: Summarise a sample's results as <sample>_personal_report.html, .md and .json
plus a findings table, from the result manifests in its folder.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--input`, `-i` | BAM, CRAM or VCF of the sample: only its runs (and runs on files made from it) are reported. Its folder holds the results unless workspace is given. |
| `workspace` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--workspace` | Sample folder whose results are reported (default: the --genome folder, else the --input's folder). |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the sample folder). |
| `results` | `tuple[Path, ...]` | `[]` | `--results` | Also read result manifests from this folder (repeatable); only runs on this sample's files are used. The --outdir is always read. |
| `table_format` | `str` | `'tsv'` | `--format` | Format of the findings table, <sample>_personal_report_findings.tsv or .parquet (needs pyarrow) (default: tsv) One of: `tsv`, `parquet` |

## `api.sample`

`sample`: show and correct what is recorded about a sample in its
workspace, `wgsextract.sample.toml` (see docs/sample-workspace.md).

### `api.sample.show(SampleShowParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract sample show`.

Read the workspace. `details` holds `genome_folder`, the
folder-wide `overrides`, `files` (each recorded file's `status` —
current, changed or missing — its detected `facts` and its own
`overrides` with their `status` and `values`),
`outputs` and, with an input, `effective`: the facts in effect for it,
each with its `source` (override or detected).

`SampleShowParams`: Show a sample's overrides, the facts recorded for each of its files and
the result manifests indexed in its workspace.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--input`, `-i` | BAM, CRAM or VCF of the sample; its folder is the workspace unless workspace is given, and its facts are shown. |
| `workspace` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--workspace` | Sample folder holding wgsextract.sample.toml (default: the --genome folder, else the --input's folder). |

### `api.sample.set_overrides(SampleSetParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract sample set`.

Set overrides; `details` is the workspace afterwards, as `show`.

`SampleSetParams`: Set overrides: facts commands use instead of what they detect. A sex
override is folder-wide in a genome folder (one person's files); anything
else, and every platform override, is for the `input` file alone and
lapses when that file changes. Commands still detect an overridden fact
cheaply and warn when the reads disagree.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--input`, `-i` | BAM, CRAM or VCF of the sample; its folder is the workspace unless workspace is given, and its facts are shown. |
| `workspace` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--workspace` | Sample folder holding wgsextract.sample.toml (default: the --genome folder, else the --input's folder). |
| `sex` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--sex` | The sample's sex (m and f are accepted too); for the whole genome folder, else for --input only. One of: `Male`, `Female` |
| `platform` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--platform` | The sequencing platform of --input (nanopore, hifi, mgi and bgi are accepted too). One of: `illumina`, `ont`, `pacbio`, `ultima`, `dnbseq` |

### `api.sample.unset_overrides(SampleUnsetParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract sample unset`.

Remove overrides; `details` is the workspace afterwards, as `show`.

`SampleUnsetParams`: Remove overrides, so commands detect those facts again: the
folder-wide one and, with `input`, that file's own.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--input`, `-i` | BAM, CRAM or VCF of the sample; its folder is the workspace unless workspace is given, and its facts are shown. |
| `workspace` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--workspace` | Sample folder holding wgsextract.sample.toml (default: the --genome folder, else the --input's folder). |
| `sex` | `bool` | `False` | `--sex` | Remove the sex override. |
| `platform` | `bool` | `False` | `--platform` | Remove the platform override. |

## `api.support`

`report-issue`: a pre-filled, redacted GitHub bug report.

`build_issue_report` collects this installation's versions, OS, CPU, RAM,
tools and settings and, by default, the last run recorded on this computer
(command line, exit status, error, warnings, log tail), redacts them, and
fits them into a GitHub new-issue link:

```python
report = api.support.build_issue_report(api.ReportIssueParams(last_failed=True))
print(report.body)                     # review it
api.support.open_issue(report)         # the user submits it on GitHub
```

Nothing is uploaded: the link opens GitHub's new-issue form in the browser,
where the user reviews and submits it. Reports never contain genotypes, reads,
file contents, sample, user or computer names, full paths or secrets.

### `api.support.build_issue_report(ReportIssueParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract report-issue`.

Collect, redact and fit a report; writes nothing and opens nothing.

`result` reports on that run (e.g. one the API just returned) instead of
`params.run` or the last recorded run. Raises `UsageError` when
`params.run` is not a readable manifest, run log or provenance file.

`ReportIssueParams`: Build a redacted GitHub bug report about this installation and a run
(by default the last one recorded on this computer).

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `run` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--run` | Report on this run: a result manifest (*.manifest.json), a run log (*.log) or its *.provenance.json (default: the last run). |
| `last_failed` | `bool` | `False` | `--last-failed` | Report on the last failed run instead of the last run. |
| `title` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--title` | Issue title (default: the command and its exit code; the error goes in the body). |
| `description` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--description` | What you did and what went wrong, for the 'What happened?' field. |
| `log_lines` | `int` | `40` | `--log-lines` | Log lines to include, from the end (default: 40). |
| `max_url_length` | `int` | `8000` | `--max-url-length` | Longest link to produce; diagnostics are shortened to fit (default: 8000; at least 1000). |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder to save the full report in (default: 'reports' in the per-user data folder). |

### `api.support.reports_directory() -> Path`

Where reports are saved by default: `reports` in the state directory
(the `state_directory` setting, else `state` in the data folder).

### `api.support.issue_url(report: IssueReport, *, max_length: int = 8000) -> str`

The new-issue link for `report` after editing its `title`,
`description` or `link_diagnostics` (`dataclasses.replace`); the
diagnostics are cut at a line if the link would exceed `max_length`.

### `api.support.save_issue_report(report: IssueReport, directory: Path | None = None) -> Path`

Save the full redacted report (`report.body`) as Markdown in
`directory` (default: `reports` in the per-user data folder).

### `api.support.open_issue(report: IssueReport) -> bool`

Open `report.url` in the browser; False when no browser could start.
Only call this after the user has seen the report and agreed.

### `api.support.IssueReport`

A redacted bug report, ready to show the user and open on GitHub.

`diagnostics` is the full redacted text, saved locally by
`save`; `link_diagnostics` is what fits in `url` (see
`truncated`). Edit `title`, `description` or `link_diagnostics`
with `dataclasses.replace` and call `issue_url` for a new link.

- `body`: The whole issue as Markdown, as saved in the diagnostics file.
- `save`: Write `body` to `directory/file_name` (readable only by the user).
